You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

message.reasoning:
The question asks which team owned the notifier on 2026-02-03.

Memory entries about notifier ownership:
- The notifier is owned by team Boreal as of 2026-04-06, valid 2026-04-06 to now.
- Earlier: The notifier is owned by team Cinder as of 2026-03-17, valid 2026-03-17 to 2026-04-06.

For 2026-02-03, the latest entry that covers it is "owned by team Cinder as of 2026-03-17"? No wait — that's valid 2026-03-17 to 2026-04-06. 2026-02-03 is before 2026-03-17. Hmm.

The entries only go back to 2026-03-17. There is no entry covering notifier ownership before 2026-03-17. So the memory does not contain the answer for 2026-02-03.

Wait, do we extrapolate? The rule says answer only from memory. The earliest notifier ownership record is 2026-03-17 (Cinder). 2026-02-03 predates that. There's no entry stating ownership before 2026-03-17. So strictly, I don't know.

But one might argue "owned by Cinder as of 2026-03-17" implies it was Cinder until changed on 2026-04-06, but does it say it was owned by Cinder before 2026-03-17? "As of 2026-03-17" means the state at that date; valid from 2026-03-17 to 2026-04-06. Before that, unknown. So the answer should be "I don't know".

Hmm, but many such QA setups would expect extrapolation backward? The instructions say answer for the moment the question asks about; memory entries have validity ranges. The validity range of the Cinder entry starts 2026-03-17, which doesn't include 2026-02-03. So I don't know.
